answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted attestation with a slow reputation mirror: each agent must lock a deposit that only grows back through useful, peer-attested work, so a gale of fresh sock-puppet identities starts at zero trust and earns nothing by volume alone. Like water carving karst, trust accumulates slowly through verifiable history, while a sybil flood faces the same deposit and waiting cost per identity — multiplying identities multiplies the bill, not the reward.
